# Agent OS — Architecture  Most agent stacks hardcode a model name into every call site. Agent OS does the opposite. A capability is a seat — a logical slot like fast, reader, coder, or judge — and each seat self-reports the task KINDS it can serve. The router builds a by_kind index at runtime and resolves kind → capable seat on every task, so swapping providers, adding a local model, or wiring an MCP tool never touches your call sites. Around that router sits a kernel that runs a goal in cycles

# Bugbot — Architecture  Bugbot reviews unified diffs, not whole repos. A FINDER model traces data flow and error paths across the changed hunks and proposes candidate findings under strict noise rules (no style, no nits — only logic bugs, leaks, races, broken error handling, security, and contract breaks). Every candidate then faces a REFUTER: a second adversarial pass whose default verdict is KILL and which must fail to disprove a finding before it surfaces. Findings arrive as structured JSON

# Fusion — Architecture  Fusion is a front door for LLM work that picks the cheapest lane that still gets the right answer. Trivial tasks go to a single model. Homogeneous batches run speculative batch-fusion — draft cheap, verify the whole block in one judge pass, re-work only what fails. Hard or high-stakes tasks get the full panel: an author drafts, a second model cross-watches and refines, and a judge does a final correctness-and-elevate pass. # Output Speed — Architecture  Output Speed encodes a simple truth: LLM wall-clock scales roughly linearly with the tokens you ask a model to emit. So the biggest free speedup is emitting fewer of them. budgetFor(kind) right-sizes max_tokens per task kind (a classification never gets a 4000-token budget; a code file never gets starved below its floor). fastLane(kind) names the fastest seat that is still capable of the kind — mechanical work on a fast low-effort seat, judging on a strong one. tri

# MYRIAD — Architecture  MYRIAD is self-play for LLM agents. Given a task, it proposes K attempts along fixed, distinct reasoning angles, fans them out through any model you inject, scores each with a DETERMINISTIC verifier you control (never a model grading its own work), and computes each attempt's group-relative advantage with critic-free GRPO. The best variant is the answer; the spread becomes a lesson you can distill into a policy. No gradient step, no training loop, no judge model — just s

# LLM Split — Architecture  LLM Split solves a mundane, expensive problem: you have two ways to run inference — a metered API and a flat-rate plan, two subscriptions, two accounts — and you want the fleet's volume held to a deliberate ratio instead of drifting wherever habit takes it. Instrument your client choke points with record(side), and every call in the fleet is counted into a daily ledger regardless of which script made it. When a caller can go either way, pickSide() answers with the sid

# Megacycle — Architecture  Megacycle is a continuous self-improvement engine for a codebase. Each round it runs a fleet of tiny, $0, local scanners in parallel — test coverage, doc freshness, dependency drift, TODO/FIXME debt, untested files — each of which reads real on-disk state and PREDICTS the highest-leverage builds to do next. A Consumable represents a physical consumable that has a manufacturer, product ID, type, etc., and is used to create a Consumable Pool. This allows for standardization between projects so that you don't wind up with 42 different variations of the same product.
